topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by connecting it to the practicals and outlining its learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how studies of tumor-causing viruses established that cancer can originate through changes to normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experiments test whether genes and mutations confer transformed properties on cells.

topics.label: Functional classification and effects of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects, using cell-cycle regulation and p53 to demonstrate and qualify those classifications.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defective DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish sequence instability from chromosomal instability and explain how failures of DNA repair produce these abnormalities.

topics.label: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how errors in copying and segregating the genome generate instability that can support tumor adaptation.

topics.label: Mutation order in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing and order of mutation acquisition influence colorectal tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and BRCA2-deficient tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow the consequences of inherited tumor-suppressor mutations from increased cancer risk to the evolution of a BRCA2-deficient tumor during treatment.

topics.label: Lecture close, further reading, and questions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by inviting questions, recommending reading, and introducing the next lecture.
